title: Determination of lignin in lignocellulosic biomass
author: Magdiel Láinez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bumtnu6n

steps.title: Prepare biomass sample
steps.instruction: Mill the dried biomass to a particle size of 0.250–0.425 mm; if needed, wash the material with distilled water to remove starch, gums and non‑structural carbohydrates, then dry the biomass.

substeps.instruction: Wash with distilled water (if required) to remove starch, gums, non‑structural carbohydrates

steps.title: Weigh dry biomass
steps.instruction: Accurately weigh 300 mg of the dried biomass into an assay tube.

steps.title: Acid hydrolysis
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of 72 % H₂SO₄ to the assay tube, homogenize with a glass rod or magnetic stirrer, and place the tube in a water bath at 30 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Dilute acid mixture
steps.instruction: Transfer the hydrolysate to a glass bottle and add exactly 84 mL of distilled water (use an analytical balance) to obtain a 4 % H₂SO₄ solution; the total mass of biomass plus 4 % acid should be 89.19 g.

steps.title: Filter and collect lignin
steps.instruction: Autoclave a glass Gooch crucible (type F), record its weight, filter the diluted mixture through the crucible (or a 0.45 µm MCE membrane filter); retain the lignin in the crucible, collect the filtrate for carbohydrate analysis by HPLC, and wash the retained lignin to remove residual acid.

steps.title: Dry crucible to constant weight
steps.instruction: Dry the glass Gooch crucible (or MCE filter) containing the lignin until a constant weight is reached.

steps.title: Determine lignin content
steps.instruction: Weigh the dried crucible with lignin and calculate lignin content as the weight difference between the crucible before and after lignin retention.
